story: The Gateway Arch is 630 feet tall and 630 feet wide at its base, a weighted catenary curve of stainless steel over a concrete and steel core. The architect Eero Saarinen won the design competition for it in the late 1940s, and it was completed in 1965. Small tram cars ride up inside its legs to a viewing chamber at the top.

The park began in 1935 as the Jefferson National Expansion Memorial, set on the site of the original city along the Mississippi. It commemorates Thomas Jefferson's Louisiana Purchase and the westward journeys that began here, including the Lewis and Clark expedition — and the museum beneath the arch also tells of what that expansion cost the Native nations of the West.

A few blocks west stands the Old Courthouse. In 1846 Dred and Harriet Scott, enslaved, sued there for their freedom. Their case reached the US Supreme Court, whose 1857 ruling against them deepened the divide that led to the Civil War.
The memorial was renamed Gateway Arch National Park in 2018, the year a new museum and landscaped grounds connecting the arch to downtown opened.

entrances: The visitor center and museum entrance faces west, toward the Old Courthouse and downtown
planYourVisit.reservations: Tram rides to the top are timed and often sell out, especially in summer and on weekends. Book ahead.
lodging: Downtown St. Louis hotels, a short walk away

chronology.text: Dred and Harriet Scott file suit for their freedom at the Old Courthouse.
The Supreme Court rules against the Scotts in Dred Scott v. Sandford.
The Jefferson National Expansion Memorial is established.
Eero Saarinen's design wins the memorial's architectural competition.
The memorial is renamed Gateway Arch National Park.

safety: The tram cars are small and enclosed. Visitors uneasy in tight spaces may prefer the museum and the riverfront.
regulations: Bags are screened at the entrance to the arch.
Drones may not be launched, landed or flown in the park.

fees.detail: Prices vary by date of visit. Begin your tour with an interactive pre-boarding experience featuring 60s-inspired animation and Gateway Arch trivia. Then, be transported 630 feet to the top of Arch for exhilarating views. Please allow 45 - 60 minutes for your Tram Ride to the Top experience. Adult (16 and up): Starting at $15 Child (3-15): Starting at $11 Infant (2 and under): FREE Park Pass Holder: Starting at $12 Tickets available at www.gatewayarch.com

operatingHours: The Gateway Arch is open year-round, closed only on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year’s Day. Summer Hours (9am-6pm, Sunday through Thursday and 9am-8pm Friday and Saturday) run the Friday before Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend and are the primary visitor season. During Regular Hours (the day after Labor Day through Friday before Memorial Day) we are open from 9am to 6pm. Around the holidays we occasionally have extended hours.
